title: DIAS: Distance-based Attention Sparsity for Ultra-Long-Sequence Transformer with Tree-like Processing-in-Memory Architecture
problem: Transformer decode stage suffers from memory bandwidth bottleneck in attention and massive KV cache memory overhead; conventional attention sparsity methods degrade accuracy on ultra-long sequences (>1M tokens).
motivation: Long-context LLM inference is critical for applications but memory bandwidth and capacity are fundamental bottlenecks; sparsity must maintain accuracy while reducing computation and data movement.
method: Instead of computing attention (relevance between all token pairs) for every position, the method only computes it fully for nearby tokens and uses approximate top-K search (AKAttention) to select important distant ones, reducing computation significantly. The key-value cache needed during decoding is stored in a tree-structured processing-in-memory architecture (TreePIM), where computation happens inside memory units rather than moving data to the processor, improving both memory capacity and access speed.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using distance to select which token pairs to compute attention for, combined with a hierarchical processing-in-memory architecture for storing the key-value cache, while maintaining accuracy on ultra-long sequences over 1 million tokens.
contributions: Approximate top-K attention scoring via graph-based search
TreePIM architecture: scalable hierarchical processing-in-memory for KV cache
75x speedup vs SOTA LLM accelerators on 1M sequence Llama3-405B with <1% accuracy drop
limitations: Evaluation limited to Llama3-405B; generalization to other models and sequence length scaling behavior not explored.
primary_theme: Distance-based attention sparsity with hierarchical PIM for ultra-long LLM inference
